subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 27, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 27, 2026

Development continues at a steady pace with significant fixes landing in our ISO builds this week. Darren merged a critical kms hook addition to the live initramfs configuration that resolves the NVIDIA no-signal boot issue affecting some users on first launch. The same fix has been applied to both the main AcreetionOS repository and the XLibre variant, ensuring consistent hardware compatibility across our distribution flavors.

A welcome quality-of-life improvement arrived with the bottom panel icon clickability fix, addressing a persistent UI annoyance where taskbar icons were unresponsive. Natalie's initial commit to the new acreetionos-wallpapers repository signals fresh artwork coming soon for desktop customization enthusiasts. The welcome-screen module also received updates restoring missing functionality and polishing the first-boot experience.

Behind the scenes, our CI/CD pipelines have been processing security updates from upstream Arch and AlmaLinux, including patches for critical packages like ghostscript, firewalld, and freerdp. The fences utility saw a resizing bug squashed, improving window management stability on Cinnamon. These incremental fixes collectively strengthen the foundation ahead of our next point release.

Community News brings recognition for open-source contributor Dave Täht, who received the prestigious Jonathan B. Postel Service Award from the Internet Society. His work on bufferbloat reduction and network performance has influenced countless projects including our own kernel tuning approaches. We celebrate this well-deserved honor for a developer whose contributions make the internet faster for everyone.

System76 released Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS this week, showcasing the continued vitality of the Ubuntu-based ecosystem. While we chart our own Arch-based course, healthy competition among Linux distributions drives innovation that benefits all users. Their COSMIC desktop progress remains worth watching for cross-pollination ideas.

Our Discord community has been active with installation success stories and hardware compatibility reports following the recent ISO refresh. Several users confirmed the NVIDIA boot fix works on RTX 30 and 40 series cards. New members from the Pop!_OS release announcement thread have discovered AcreetionOS and joined our conversations about Arch-based alternatives.

Tips & Highlights: If you're experiencing display detection issues on live boot, the new kms hook should resolve them automatically in the latest ISO. For existing installations, running mkinitcpio -P after updating will apply the fix without reinstalling. This is especially relevant for hybrid graphics laptops and external monitor setups.

The welcome screen now includes a direct link to our hardware compatibility wiki page, which we've expanded with community-submitted reports this month. Checking this resource before installing can save time on driver configuration. We encourage users to submit their own hardware results to keep the database current.
